reviews.text:
Partner Perspective - More Frustrating Than Useful. Having a calendar of my partner’s cycle and knowing potential symptoms are great. The app UI and the way one must navigate to get this information is god awful. 

1. Notifications - just straight up bad. So much useless garbage on “how to ask my partner x” or “why do my balls hurt”. This is not why I signed up for the app. Help me get ahead of potential challenges for HER or leave me alone. 

2. The calendar. You need to go to another screen just to see a key of what the different dots mean. Terrible UX. It also only warns of when period days actually are. I would rather visibility on Ludial phase days - you know, when a lot of women are really starting to hurt and their partners SHOULD be made aware of how to help. This is where the Flo app has caused friction in the relationship - I don’t actually have the visibility I need. 

3. The little “story card” presentation is annoying, unpredictable, and makes the user feel rushed. The “her symptoms” card doesn’t always show and is timed on how long you can look at it. The info disappears and requires tapping backwards or forwards to revisit it. Just terrible. Imagine if you were at work and someone timed how long you could look at infographic with key information. There are a dozen of other issues with this format that just make it feel annoying and almost hostile.

reviews.text:
Not worth the money. I used to really enjoy this app because it felt like a helpful tool for tracking women’s health and fertility. Unfortunately, it seems like more and more features are being locked behind a paywall. Women’s health information, cycle tracking, and fertility support should be accessible, not something that constantly requires another subscription or upgrade.

What was once a useful resource now feels more focused on making money than helping users. At this point, I don’t see enough value in paying for features that used to be free or that can easily be replaced by my phone’s calendar, my OB-GYN, or my primary care provider.

It’s disappointing to see a platform that was once genuinely helpful become so heavily centered around monetization. I understand businesses need revenue, but when nearly every useful feature comes with a price tag, it takes away from the overall experience. I expected support for women’s health, not a constant push to subscribe.
